lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the project pool by the three-stamen rule, inferior 3-locular ovary, equitant/2-ranked leaves and rhipidiate spathe-bracted inflorescences, then split Sisyrinchium from Nemastylis.

project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas family-first module across Sisyrinchium and Nemastylis
project_scope.note: The five project taxa provide a strong grasslike-leaf versus pleated-bulb contrast while sharing the same Iridaceae reproductive plan.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: On a grasslike or sword-leaved monocot, inspect the flower for 6 tepals but only 3 fertile stamens. Then confirm an inferior 3-locular ovary below the tepals and a capsular fruit.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Perennial herbs from rhizomes, corms or bulbs. Leaves are often basal or 2-ranked and equitant, with flattened swordlike or grasslike blades; Nemastylis leaves are distinctly pleated.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers have 6 tepals in two whorls and only 3 stamens, positioned opposite the outer tepals. Ovary is inferior and usually 3-locular. Style branches are often conspicuous and important for genus recognition.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A loculicidal capsule with many seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Six tepals + three stamens + inferior ovary is the strongest family package. The three-stamen count is especially useful against Amaryllidaceae/Asparagaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: 2-ranked/equitant leaf base → 6 tepals → 3 stamens → inferior ovary → spathes/rhipidium → Sisyrinchium-vs-Nemastylis
visual_lesson.intro: Blue-eyed grasses are not grasses. Count the stamens: the iris-family flower runs on three.

steps.title: 1 · Look at the leaf bases, not just the blade
steps.look_for: Flattened leaves arranged in two ranks, with overlapping/sheathing bases; Nemastylis adds obvious pleating.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the vegetative doorway before flowers open.

steps.title: 2 · Count six tepals but only three stamens
steps.look_for: Six petaloid tepals surrounding exactly three fertile stamens.
steps.why_it_matters: The 3-stamen rule is one of the best family-level characters in local Asparagales.

steps.title: 3 · Find the ovary below the flower
steps.look_for: Inferior 3-locular ovary sitting below the point where tepals and stamens attach.
steps.why_it_matters: Pairs with the 3-stamen count to separate Iridaceae from many superficially similar monocots.

steps.title: 4 · Read the spathes and rhipidium
steps.look_for: Flowers emerging sequentially from opposed green spathes in a flattened rhipidiate inflorescence.
steps.why_it_matters: A high-value structure for both Sisyrinchium and Nemastylis.

steps.title: 5 · Sisyrinchium door: grasslike but with iris flowers
steps.look_for: Flattened often winged scapelike stems, equitant narrow leaves, small blue/purple/yellow-centered flowers, 3 stamens and a globose capsule.
steps.why_it_matters: Explains why 'blue-eyed grass' is an iris relative, not a grass.

steps.title: 6 · Nemastylis door: pleated leaves + threadlike split styles
steps.look_for: Bulbous geophyte with pleated leaves, blue spreading tepals, and each of three style branches deeply divided into two threadlike arms extending around the anthers.
steps.why_it_matters: The style architecture is an exceptionally distinctive genus character.

comparisons.title: Iridaceae vs Amaryllidaceae
comparisons.rule: Iridaceae has 3 fertile stamens and an inferior ovary. Project Amaryllidaceae has 6 stamens; Allium/Nothoscordum have superior ovaries while Zephyranthes has an inferior ovary.

comparisons.title: Iridaceae vs Asparagaceae
comparisons.rule: Both may have 6 tepals, but local Asparagaceae/Yucca has 6 stamens and usually a different rosette/panicle architecture; Iridaceae has 3 stamens and an inferior ovary.

comparisons.title: Iridaceae vs Orchidaceae
comparisons.rule: Both typically have inferior ovaries, but orchids are strongly specialized with a labellum and reproductive column, commonly only one fertile stamen; Iridaceae retains 6 tepals and 3 ordinary fertile stamens.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not identify Iridaceae from swordlike leaves alone. The reproductive confirmation is 3 stamens + inferior ovary.

genera.fast_cue: equitant narrow leaves + flattened/winged stems + small iris-like flowers + 3 stamens
bulb + pleated leaves + large blue spreading flower + deeply bifid threadlike style branches

family_confusion_polish.look_here_first: Count three fertile stamens and locate the inferior ovary below tepal insertion. Six tepals alone do not prove iris family: Zephyranthes also has an inferior ovary but six stamens. Inspect equitant leaf bases, flattened stems and spathe-enclosed sequential flowers as supporting characters.
family_confusion_polish.comparison: Iridaceae (Sisyrinchium, Nemastylis): three stamens and inferior ovary. Amaryllidaceae (Allium, Nothoscordum, Zephyranthes): six stamens; superior ovary in the onion genera, inferior in rain lilies. Poaceae has spikelets with glumes, lemma and palea rather than six showy tepals. Orchidaceae has a reproductive column and labellum.
family_confusion_polish.genus_routing: Sisyrinchium: equitant leaf bases, flattened/winged stem, small flower with three stamens; Nemastylis: pleated leaves and three style branches each deeply split into two slender arms. Verify flower anatomy rather than color.
